period: Dates are highly uncertain; scholars' estimates for the Vaisheshika Sutras range from several centuries BCE to the early centuries CE.
context: Kanada is traditionally the author of the Vaisheshika Sutras, the root text of the Vaisheshika school. His name is often explained as 'atom-eater' or 'grain-gatherer', and the stories told about him are legendary. Vaisheshika developed an analysis of reality into categories and an atomic theory of matter. It later merged with Nyaya into a combined school, and Prashastapada's commentary (around the 6th century CE) became its classic exposition.
coreIdeas: Reality can be analysed into categories (padarthas): substance, quality, action, universal, particularity and inherence, with absence added later
Material things are composed of eternal, indivisible atoms
Nine substances, including the self (atman) and mind (manas), are recognised
Dharma is presented as that which leads to worldly welfare and the highest good
Knowledge of the categories contributes to liberation

disagreements.note: Vaisheshika's enduring substances, real wholes and universals, and enduring self stand against Buddhist doctrines of momentariness and no-self, and were long debated between the schools.
